newsitem.title: UK: Options-Vols pop up on gold OTC nearby dates.
newsitem.headline: Options-Vols pop up on gold OTC nearby dates.

text.p: Volatilites on nearby September OTC gold options have jumped modestly over the past few days on increased buying interest, dealers said.
Bids for September at-the-money options climbed from bids around 3.5 percent volatility early last week to 4.5 and 5.0 percent.
"There's a little more buying around at the moment, I guess on fears that we could see a spike in gold," a London dealer said.
Some players feared a move after an IMF decision on selling reserves, but did not know which way, so they were buying strangles placed at the borders of the current $380-$385 range.
A European dealer said most of the interest he saw was for puts under $380. Some people short of options may be tidying up their positions, another dealer suggested.
Others were probably attracted by volatilities at extremely low rates.
"At 4.0 percent it's almost impossible to lose money. people are reasonably happy to buy at these levels...If you get an 85-cent move per day you make money," a dealer said.
The increase in volatilities was only seen on the September options, which expire next Thursday, and activity was routine in the other dates, with volatilities stable.
After the expiry, one dealer expected pressure to reappear in October options. "The Septs have recovered, but it's not exactly off to the races."
October at-the-money volatilities were bid at 4.7 to 5.0 percent, three months at 5.2 to 5.5 percent, six months at 6.0 to 6.25 percent and one year options at 6.75 to 7.0 percent.
The market was looking forward to the end of the summer and more movement in the underlying market.
"I think the summer doldrums and the 50-cent-a-day moves are probably gone now. As we get into October we'll see slightly wider ranges," a dealer said.
